claim.text: Holding Python 3.11, one CPU runner, and exact serialized LMMSE inputs fixed, PyTorch 2.9.1 and 2.10.0 agree byte-for-byte on the tested finite outputs.
claim.scope: One AMD EPYC 7763 AVX2 GitHub VM, 6 selected synthetic fixtures, 2 whitening modes, 3 repeats each, Python 3.11.18 throughout; no GPU or physical RF data.
assumptions: One GitHub VM within all A-B-A stages
SHA256-verified frozen original and transformed complex tensors
Identical Python 3.11 interpreter build and non-Torch dependency versions
Sionna public LMMSE code and one CPU thread
High-condition cases are stress inputs, not representative RF
forbidden_promotions: No global hardware/output bitwise portability assertion
No real 6G BER/SER, throughput or sensitivity implication
No inference that AVX2 vs AVX512 alone caused earlier differences
No inference that matched solver bits imply oracle accuracy

invariants: All input SHA-256 fingerprints identical in A1/B/A2

Same-stage threefold repeatability and A1-A2 restoration

Independent represented-input posterior oracle checked for numerical accuracy

Moderate complex128 2x2 control with cov cond 30 frame cond 3

controls.sampling_parity: No sampling inside replay, immutable source and transformed input bytes
controls.data_access_parity: All stages read same checked-out frozen fixture file; per-tensor SHA256 enforced

preregistration.prediction: Changing Torch release under a fixed Python/host does not necessarily alter LMMSE result bits; A1 and A2 must agree for repeatability.
preregistration.primary_metric: Fraction of finite original+transformed output pairs byte-identical and fraction of matching failure classifications in A1-B/B-A2/A1-A2.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Exact repeated comparisons on six purposive fixtures on one GitHub CPU, no population confidence interval or independent RF measurement.
preregistration.kill_condition: Any fixture hash mismatch, Python mismatch or A1-vs-A2 instability invalidates an inference from version switch; safe case oracle failure retires safe-accuracy claim.
preregistration.stop_condition: No further synthetic expansion without upstream reviewer need or a real supported receiver trace.
preregistration.promotion_rule: Promote only measured equality for frozen inputs under this CPU/Python stack; do not claim cross-platform causality or improved PHY performance.

result.observed: On AMD EPYC 7763 AVX2 single GitHub VM with Python3.11.18 fixed, Torch2.9.1->2.10.0->2.9.1 yielded 27/27 finite repeated rows byte-identical and 36/36 state+Cholesky matches in every pairwise comparison. All 12 moderate repeated rows/stage passed independent reference tolerance; 9 high-condition rows/stage nonfinite, 9 additional finite extreme rows out of oracle tolerance. Both Torch versions recomputed all six covariance arrays byte-identical to originally frozen sp on this host, in contrast to earlier Intel/AVX512 hosted run.
result.effect_size: Zero paired finite estimate/variance absolute error; 27/27 finite repeated-row hash matches and 36/36 failure state matches in each of A1-B/B-A2/A1-A2.
result.uncertainty: Single matched GitHub VM, six purposive synthetic inputs, nine finite configurations each repeated three times. No RF representativeness or independent hardware causal isolation.
